newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt shrugs off M3 data, seen rangebound.
newsitem.headline: German debt shrugs off M3 data, seen rangebound.

text.p: German Bund and futures kicked off the week with losses but dealers predicted these would be capped with the market trading mostly in a range, worried by French politics and awaiting new U.S. economic data. "The excitement for the morning seems to be over now, and we will settle into a comfortable but narrow range," said one dealer shortly after German M3 numbers were released.

By 0818 GMT the June Bund futures contract traded on Frankfurt's DTB exchange was down 20 basis points at 100.63, having traded in a 100.81-100.55 range. Dealers predicted a 100.20 to 101.20 range for the session and the next days.

M3, once an eagerly awaited indicator, today barely moved the market, partly both because it came in as expected at 8.3 percent and because the Bundesbank itself has appeared to distance itself slightly from the key policy indicator.

"The M3 number was useless this morning," said one dealer, noting that even if the number were to move into the 3.5 to 6.5 percent target corridor this year, the Bundesbank would likely not cut its interest rates again.
Instead the market is focusing more strongly on nervousness about the spectre of early elections in France to avoid any conflicts with meeting the EMU timetable.
With the French June Notionnel down 38 basis points, dealers said some weakness had lapped into the German market as well.

Analysts cautioned that ongoing worries about Germany's EMU qualifications and speculation that the Maastricht entry criteria might have to be eased after all to secure a timely EMU start, were also weighing on the market.
On the other hand the German market also remains concerned about the direction of U.S. interest rates and is not expected to be able to decouple itself from U.S. market movements this week.
"There is nothing on in the U.S. this week, but next week there is a bunch of numbers that will be really important for the market, so we will wait until then," another dealer said.
Tuesday's German 10-year bond issue is also not expected to weigh on the market very much, dealers said.
"Alot of people have already made room for the bond," a dealer said.
Resistance levels for the Bund future are seen at 101.00 and 101.14 while support is seen around 100.60 or 100.53 today.
